title: Protect the Third Pole from mineral mining | Science
description: The global green-energy transition has led to soaring demand for critical minerals (1), placing unprecedented extraction pressure on fragile alpine ecosystems such as the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP), also known as the Third Pole, which hosts more than 3000 valuable mineral deposits (2). Most active mines in the QTP are located at altitudes exceeding 4000 m (3, 4), wheremining activities could accelerate permafrost thaw and pollute water (4) on which millions of downstream residents depend (5). On 15 May, China’s State Council passed regulations requiring local governments to investigate and assess ecological damage and environmental pollution caused by mining activities (6). Local governments in the QTP should adhere to the law by strengthening supervision and ecosystem management of mining activities.
